title: The sons request permission to preach
summary: The sons of Mosiah return to their father, the king, with a small number they selected and request permission to go to the land of Nephi to preach to the Lamanites.
characters: a small number selected by the sons

explicit_facts.text: The sons of Mosiah took a small number with them, returned to their father, the king, and requested permission to go with those selected to the land of Nephi to preach to the Lamanites.
They hoped the Lamanites might come to know the Lord their God, overcome their hatred toward the Nephites, become friendly with them, and end contentions in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sons and those accompanying them are present before the king as the request is made.
unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place, clothing, gestures, and identities of those selected.

narration.text: they took a small number with them and returned to their father, the king
and desired of him that he would grant unto them
go up to the land of Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 2 describes hoped-for outcomes, not events that have occurred in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the journey, preaching, or hoped-for outcomes as occurring here.
Do not invent direct dialogue or identify individual sons or companions.

title: Concern for every soul
summary: They desired salvation to be declared to every creature. The thought of any soul enduring endless torment caused them to quake and tremble. The Spirit of the Lord worked upon them; the Lord spared them, and they suffered anguish because of their iniquities and feared being cast off forever.

explicit_facts.text: They desired salvation to be declared to every creature and could not bear that any human soul should perish.
The thought of any soul enduring endless torment caused them to quake and tremble.
The Spirit of the Lord worked upon them, and the Lord spared them in mercy.
They suffered anguish of soul because of their iniquities and feared being cast off forever.

reasonable_visual_inferences: They may be shown trembling, as the text describes.
A distressed posture may convey their narrated anguish.
unspecified_visual_details: Their identities, number, clothing, surroundings, and exact expressions.

narration.text: they were desirous that salvation should be declared to every creature
they suffered much anguish of soul because of their iniquities

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Spirit’s work, the Lord’s mercy, and the feared torment are narrated; no visible manifestation is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign individual names or depict a literal vision of torment or a visible divine figure.

title: Pleading over many days
summary: They plead with their father over many days to go to the land of Nephi.
characters: Those pleading (unnamed in the supplied verse)
Their father (unnamed in the supplied verse)

explicit_facts.text: They pleaded with their father many days so that they might go to the land of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Those pleading and their father may be shown together during one of the pleas.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearances, the setting, gestures, and the words of any individual plea.

narration.text: they did plead with their father many days that they might go up to the land of Nephi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse summarizes pleading over many days; it does not describe a particular exchange.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names to the participants, invent dialogue, or specify the number of visits.

title: Mosiah inquires of the Lord
summary: King Mosiah inquires of the Lord whether to let his sons preach among the Lamanites. The Lord tells him to let them go and promises that many will believe, have eternal life, and that his sons will be delivered from the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: King Mosiah inquired of the Lord whether to let his sons go among the Lamanites to preach the word.
The Lord told Mosiah to let his sons go, said many would believe their words and have eternal life, and promised to deliver his sons from the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown inquiring; the Lord's answer need not be accompanied by a visible form.
unspecified_visual_details: The place of inquiry and how the Lord communicates.

spoken_dialogue.text: Let them go up, for many shall believe on their words, and they shall have eternal life; and I will deliver thy sons out of the hands of the Lamanites.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the Lord

narration.text: And king Mosiah went and inquired of the Lord if he should let his sons go up among the Lamanites to preach the word.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Present the narration of Mosiah's inquiry before the Lord's reply.
The Lord's promises are spoken, not shown as fulfilled.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible form of the Lord; none is described.
Do not depict the sons preaching or being delivered in this scene.

title: Journey into the wilderness
summary: Mosiah granted their request. They then journeyed into the wilderness to preach the word among the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah granted that they might go and do according to their request.
They took their journey into the wilderness to preach the word among the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The travelers may be shown entering the wilderness; Mosiah's earlier grant need not be depicted as a simultaneous event.
unspecified_visual_details: The travelers' identities and number, their appearance, their departure point, and their route.

narration.text: Mosiah granted that they might go and do according to their request.
And they took their journey into the wilderness to go up to preach the word among the Lamanites;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Preaching among the Lamanites is the purpose of the journey; no preaching encounter is narrated in these verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the travelers by name or add companions.
Do not depict arrival among the Lamanites or later proceedings.

title: No son accepts the kingdom
summary: Mosiah has no one to whom to confer the kingdom because none of his sons will accept it.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah had no one to confer the kingdom upon, because none of his sons would accept the kingdom.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether Mosiah is alone or with others, the setting, and any physical representation of the kingdom.

narration.text: there was not any of his sons who would accept of the kingdom

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a narrated circumstance, not a scene of the sons refusing in person.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a new refusal or depict the sons present.

title: Mosiah gathers the records
summary: Mosiah takes the brass-plate records, the plates of Nephi, and the things he had preserved. He does so because his people greatly desire to learn about a people who had been destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah took the records engraved on the brass plates, the plates of Nephi, and the things he had kept and preserved according to God's commandments.
Before this, Mosiah had translated and caused to be written the records on gold plates found by Limhi's people and delivered to him by Limhi.
Mosiah acted because his people greatly desired to know about the people who had been destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown handling plates and records as he takes them.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, arrangement, and appearance of the records and plates are unspecified.

narration.text: he took the records which were engraven on the plates of brass
And this he did because of the great anxiety of his people; for they were desirous beyond measure to know concerning those people who had been destroyed.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The translation and Limhi's delivery are prior events, not actions occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Limhi delivering the plates or Mosiah translating them as part of this scene.
Do not depict the destroyed people or invent details of their destruction.

title: Mosiah translates with the interpreters
summary: Mosiah translates the records using two stones fastened into the rims of a bow. The narration explains that these interpreters were prepared from the beginning, passed down through generations, and preserved by the Lord; whoever has them is called a seer.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah translated the records using two stones fastened into the two rims of a bow.
The interpreters were prepared from the beginning and handed down from generation to generation to interpret languages.
The Lord preserved them so that they could reveal the iniquities and abominations of the people to whoever possessed the land.
Whoever has these things is called a seer, after the manner of old times.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah is shown using the described stones and bow-rims as he translates.
unspecified_visual_details: The stones' appearance, the exact construction of the bow-rims, the writing surface, and Mosiah's surroundings.

narration.text: he translated them by the means of those two stones
fastened into the two rims of a bow
whosoever has these things is called seer

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage describes translation and the interpreters' purpose; do not add visible supernatural effects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show an unmentioned divine appearance or invented magical effects.

title: The translated account spans ages
summary: The translated account tells of the destroyed people from their destruction back to the building of the great tower and the scattering of the people, and further back to the creation of Adam.

explicit_facts.text: After Mosiah finished translating, the account covered the destroyed people from their destruction back to the building of the great tower, the confounding of language and scattering of people, and back to the creation of Adam.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown with the translated records as the narration describes their contents.
unspecified_visual_details: The destroyed people, tower, scattering, and Adam are mentioned in the account but are not specified as visible in the present scene.

narration.text: after Mosiah had finished translating these records
it gave an account of the people who were destroyed

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The historical events are contents of a record, not present-tense events enacted in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the tower, scattering, creation, or destruction as current visual events.

title: The people mourn and rejoice in knowledge
summary: The account causes the people of Mosiah to mourn and fills them with sorrow. It gives them much knowledge, in which they rejoice.

explicit_facts.text: The account caused the people of Mosiah to mourn and filled them with sorrow.
The account gave them much knowledge, in which they rejoiced.
The account shall be written hereafter so that all people may know what is written in it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people's expressions or postures may convey sorrow and rejoicing.
unspecified_visual_details: Which individuals are shown, the setting, and how the account is presented.

narration.text: Now this account did cause the people of Mosiah to mourn exceedingly, yea, they were filled with sorrow; nevertheless it gave them much knowledge, in the which they did rejoice.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The account's future writing is stated, not depicted as an event in this scene.
The verses do not establish that Mosiah is present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict specific events from the account, an unmentioned writing session, or Mosiah as present.

title: Mosiah entrusts the records to Alma
summary: After completing these matters, Mosiah confers the brass plates, the other preserved things, all the records, and the interpreters upon Alma, son of Alma. He commands Alma to preserve them and keep a record of the people for future generations.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah conferred the brass plates, preserved things, all the records, and interpreters upon Alma, son of Alma.
Mosiah commanded Alma to preserve them and keep a record of the people, handing records down through generations as they had been handed down since Lehi left Jerusalem.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah and Alma are present as the records and interpreters are entrusted to Alma.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise setting, words of the command, and physical appearance or arrangement of the items.

narration.text: conferred them upon him
commanded him that he should keep and preserve them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Lehi is referenced as the start of the record-keeping lineage but is not present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Lehi or invent a spoken command.
